column1: # The layout of the SASS instruction word: where each field of the 128-bit word starts, and how many bits it holds. The
# tool khw_write reads it to write the field rows of the .ksc of the part. The register walk and the predicate walk read
# those rows (orior_klq_identity). The file sass_assemble.c fills the same places.
# - `field <name> <first> <bits>`: a place in the instruction word, in bits, with a tab between each two fields.
# The offset of a constant, the offset of an address, and the descriptor of a memory operand carry what this row has
# no column for. That is a scale, or the bit that tells whether the listing shows the descriptor. They sit in
# the guard predicate: three bits its number, and the bit above them its negation
# the register places, in the order an instruction fills them
# - `pl`: that of a load, which holds its number inverted
# - `pg`: the predicate that an operation writes, and `po` the second that it writes
# the immediates: a word, and a byte above the registers
# the bit that yields the part to another warp, which the vendor's reader calls illegal set beside the longest stall
